headline: Cole Knuble, son of Mike, makes NHL debut with Flyers he grew up rooting for
take:
Per ESPN, Cole Knuble, son of former Flyers forward Mike Knuble, made his NHL debut with Philadelphia, the team he grew up rooting for. ESPN notes he has fond memories of the Flyers' home arena from his father's long career there.

The debut arrives for a club in a rough spot. Philadelphia is 1-6-3 with 5 points through 10 games, and the early numbers say the record is not just bad luck. The Flyers have generated 38.3% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality, with 50% meaning an even fight) so far this season, and at five-on-five that drops to 34%. They are being outplayed, not just outscored. Their goals are also 8.5 below what their shots should have produced, so finishing has hurt them, but goaltending has not: the team's goalies have saved 3.3 goals more than expected. Special teams give little cover, with the power play creating 0.62 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allowing 0.69. For a young player stepping in, the open question is whether he can help a team that is short on quality chances, which no single debut will fix on its own.
